# Feature: Heavy block — sanity check

<!-- Generated by the project-manager tool from pm.yml. Do not edit by hand; the store is the source of truth. -->

## Goal

Sanity-check candidate mechanic #87 (Heavy block) from Blocks before it is used in real levels. Effect: Takes two pushes per tile; power gloves make it one push. Unique: a slow block whose first push only shows Jolly straining, the second moves it. Useful: pushing labour and its animation become the pressure, power gloves relieve it. Source status in the candidate file is 'revised'; it was revised from human review and is now treated as a trial candidate.

## User Story

**As a** player

**I want** takes two pushes per tile; power gloves make it one push.

**So that** pushing labour and its animation become the pressure, power gloves relieve it.

## High-Level Use Case

The player meets Heavy block for the first time in its teaching room (mech-87-heavy-block-room). Teaching moment: First room: a heavy block on the way to a switch, with a patroller crossing behind it. A player who starts pushing without watching the patrol is caught while straining on the first push and restarts the room, which teaches that the strain is real time in which other things still move. The sanity check plays that room, exercises every rule below, and records a replayable session.

## Player-Facing Behavior

- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: It moves only onto empty floor or a switch plate, exactly as a push block (81); water, deep water, void, fire and lava block it
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: First push input: Jolly shows a pushing/straining graphic and the block budges but stays, second consecutive push moves it one tile
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Time and enemies keep running while you strain
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Wearing power gloves (89) moves it in a single push

## Edge Cases & Rules

- It moves only onto empty floor or a switch plate, exactly as a push block (81); water, deep water, void, fire and lava block it
- First push input: Jolly shows a pushing/straining graphic and the block budges but stays, second consecutive push moves it one tile
- Movement/state stays deterministic: state advances only through the pure step function with recorded t_ms; a recorded session replays to the same end state.
- Restart (R / restart) restores the room to its initial state, including this mechanic.

## UI / Feedback

- The player sees Heavy block's effect happen on its tile(s) exactly as the rules above describe; no hidden state.
- Any counter, inventory or HUD impact follows the rules above; if a rule needs a counter it is shown while it matters (see Open Questions).
- Failure in the teaching room returns the player to the room start / checkpoint for an immediate retry.

- Level JSON: new Test Level mech-87-heavy-block-room (rows + legend) implementing the teaching moment above.
- Sprites/defs: reuse existing tiles where the mechanic reuses an existing tile; add a new sprite/tile def only if this mechanic introduces a new tile (confirm in the implement task).
- Source: plans/level-design/candidate-mechanics/blocks.yml mechanic #87.

## Open Questions

- Human review to honour: We would need a graphic showing Jolly pushing, otherwise how will you know its moving
- Human review to honour: I think we could then get something like power gloves to help them move these with a single push
- Human review to honour: I think power gloves could have enough effect where single blocks could be pushed into a line - This would be domino blocks.
- Synergies deferred to a later run (do not build now): Weight switch (29): a heavy block is the costly way to hold a distant switch.
- Demos deferred (reference only): Power gloves (89, gear): before/after test room, two pushes become one.
- Confirm any new sprite/tile def and any HUD counter this mechanic needs before the implement task is approved.
